open_obligations: Check whether the claim holds beyond the single illustrative SciQ debate.
Note that no judge decides the debate; the weak model learns from transcripts.
Check whether the weak model benefits when the incorrect debater wins the exchange.
out.other_title: Central claim of debate: it is harder to lie than to refute a lie
out.rationale: Irving et al. state debate's usefulness rests on the empirical claim that it is harder to lie than to refute a lie. Lang, Huang and Li state that in their illustrative SciQ debate the incorrect debater's misleading arguments are convincingly refuted, that this conforms to Irving et al.'s claim, and that debate arguments can therefore inform weak models; the evidence offered is one example debate.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: using debate transcripts to inform weak models, relying on lies being easier to refute than to make

text: The authors state that in their illustrative debate (Figure 1) the debater assigned the incorrect answer presents misleading arguments that its opponent convincingly points out in the next turn, and say this conforms to the claim that it is harder to lie than to refute a lie, so debate arguments can inform weak models about the merits and flaws of each side.
title: Reliance on 'harder to lie than to refute a lie' (Irving et al. 2018) in debate
